sets.title: Graphite: who controls the anode?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Graphite: who controls the anode?

The biggest material in an EV battery isn't lithium.

82% of the world’s natural graphite was mined in China in 2025. (USGS MCS 2026)
~50 kg of graphite in every electric car: the largest material by weight in a lithium-ion battery. (USGS · IEA)

China refines ~90% of battery-grade graphite and ~95% of the spherical graphite used in anodes. The US imports 100% of the natural graphite it uses. Reserves are ample at ~310 Mt; the chokepoint is processing, not geology.

sets.title: Lithium: who holds the world's charge?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Lithium: who holds the world's charge?

A price that went from $11,700 to $63,700 to $9,000 in four years.

88% of the world’s lithium goes into batteries. (USGS MCS 2026)
$63,700 /t: the 2022 average price of battery-grade lithium carbonate. By 2025 it averaged $9,000. (USGS / Benchmark)

China converts ~70% of battery-grade lithium chemicals and makes more than 98% of LFP cells. A single mine, CATL’s Jianxiawo, swung the 2025–26 market when its permit lapsed in August 2025 and was renewed in June 2026.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/lithium (link in bio).

sets.title: Cobalt: whose hands power the battery age?
sets.photo_credit: Photo: artisanal cobalt miners, DRC — IIED via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.5
sets.caption:
Cobalt: whose hands power the battery age?

Nearly all cobalt is a by-product. Most of it comes from one country.

73% of the world’s cobalt was mined in the DR Congo in 2025. (USGS MCS 2026)
~79% of the world’s refined cobalt came from China in 2025. (Cobalt Institute)

Since October 2025 the DRC caps exports at 96,600 t a year, about half of 2024 volumes. Some 150,000–250,000 artisanal miners dig cobalt by hand. Cobalt-free LFP batteries already power more than half of new EVs.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/cobalt (link in bio).

sets.title: Nickel: who cornered the metal of the stainless age?
sets.photo_credit: Photo: nickel-ore mining, North Kolaka, Sulawesi — Marwan Mohamad via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
sets.caption:
Nickel: who cornered the metal of the stainless age?

Stainless steel, batteries, and a market that broke in 2022.

66% of the world’s nickel was mined in Indonesia in 2025. (USGS MCS 2026)
$100,000 /t: where nickel traded on 8 March 2022, before the LME cancelled the market. (LME)

Indonesia and China refined ~76% of the world’s nickel in 2025. Class-1 metal is only about a quarter of supply. Western mines are closing: BHP’s Nickel West is suspended and Koniambo’s furnaces have been cold since August 2024.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/nickel (link in bio).

sets.title: Rare earths: who controls the magnets?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Rare earths: who controls the magnets?

17 elements, and one supplier for the magnets in every motor and missile.

94% of sintered NdFeB magnets are made in China. (IEA)
7 of 17 rare earth elements have been under Chinese export controls since April 2025. (MOFCOM · USGS)

China handles ~91% of rare earth refining and separation. US import reliance is 67% overall and 100% for heavy rare earths. Global reserves exceed 75 Mt; the constraint is separation capacity, not geology.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/rare-earths (link in bio).

sets.title: Copper: who keeps the world wired?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Copper: who keeps the world wired?

The metal of electrification is running short of smelter feed.

$0/t the 2026 benchmark treatment charge for copper concentrate, the lowest on record. (benchmark settlement · USGS)
~30% of copper demand in 2035 is not covered by existing or announced mines. (IEA)

China refines ~48% of the world’s copper and holds ~50% of smelting capacity. LME copper hit a record $14,527.50/t in January 2026 as Cobre Panama, Grasberg and El Teniente disruptions tightened the mine side.

sets.title: Manganese: who hardens the world's steel?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Manganese: who hardens the world's steel?

Ninety percent goes into steel, and nothing else does the job.

95% of battery-grade manganese sulphate is refined in China. (IEA)
4% of the world’s manganese ore is mined in China. South Africa mines ~38%. (USGS MCS 2026)

USGS lists no satisfactory substitute for manganese in steelmaking. Gabon bans raw ore exports from 2029. Battery demand for manganese is projected to grow more than eightfold this decade.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/manganese (link in bio).

sets.title: Uranium: who fuels the nuclear revival?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Uranium: who fuels the nuclear revival?

The nuclear revival runs through Russian centrifuges.

43% of the world’s uranium enrichment capacity is Russian (Rosatom). (WNA 2025)
1 Jan 2028 when US waivers on the ban on Russian enriched uranium expire. (US law · EIA)

Kazakhstan mined ~41% of the world’s uranium in 2025. 79 reactors are under construction, 37 of them in China. Spot uranium is near $90/lb, with the long-term price at a record $95.50/lb.

sets.title: Antimony: who's playing with fire?
sets.photo_credit: NOT RECORDED on the site — confirm the header photo licence before publishing this set
sets.caption:
Antimony: who's playing with fire?

A small market with one of the thinnest reserve cushions of any strategic mineral.

>85% of the world’s antimony is mined in China, Russia and Tajikistan. (USGS MCS 2026)
$60,000 /t: the spring-2025 price peak after China began licensing exports, up from ~$12,000–14,000. (price-agency assessments)

Reserves of ~2 Mt are under two decades of supply at current mining rates. Antimony goes into flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, solar glass, ammunition primers and night-vision detectors.

Interactive map of mines, smelters and refineries, production and price charts, and the full timeline: mineral.watch/antimony (link in bio).
